prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1495; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed the center line while turning. Both drivers stated they were stopped or nearly stopped at impact. Photos requested from both parties and tow yard location confirmed. Police report number received, responding officer noted no citations issued at scene.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck stiffness and a headache since the collision and says a doctor diagnosed a concussion at urgent care. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says no one has advised them on the claim. Explained the claims process, the need for medical records, and that they may wish to seek legal advice if they have questions. Requested signed medical authorization.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed. Front bumper cover cracked, hood latch misaligned, and radiator support shows crush damage. Estimate prepared and submitted to the shop for supplemental review. Rental coverage confirmed for the claimant while repairs are in progress. Subrogation potential noted against the other carrier, pending liability confirmation.

Entry 4: Received medical records from urgent care. Diagnosis listed as concussion with post-concussive symptoms. Records recommend follow-up with a neurologist and a return visit if symptoms worsen. Claimant reports ongoing light sensitivity and difficulty concentrating at work. Reviewed records for pre-existing conditions; none noted in the file. Referred file for medical review.

Entry 5: Contacted other carrier to discuss liability. Their insured disputes fault, stating the claimant's vehicle drifted into the oncoming lane. Obtained dashcam footage from a nearby business and forwarded to the file for review. Liability remains under investigation. Diary set to follow up with the claimant on treatment status and the other carrier on their position.
